fact_cells.text: The Imamiyya hold that the Qur'an was changed, except one named man and two companions
Al-Safadi reads Ibn Hazm's exempted man as al-Sharif al-Murtada
The tahrif of speech means changing it from its places
al-Sihah, vol.4, p.31; Lisan al-Arab, vol.9, p.43
Loss of revealed text is the disputed sense of tahrif, and addition is false by consensus
The Qur'an in hand keeps the attributes God gave it, so it is the Qur'an sent down
The Qur'an Jibril brought was seventeen thousand verses
Revelation outside the Qur'an, added to it, would total seventeen thousand verses
Many sound reports state loss, and they are at least equal to the reports on the imamate
350 of al-Nuri's 1,602 reports come from al-Sayyari, whom al-Najashi calls weak in hadith
Salamat al-Qur'an, p.120; Mu'jam Rijal al-Hadith, vol.3, p.71
Reports of loss are solitary and yield neither knowledge nor grounds for action
In a sermon at Mina the Prophet ﷺ disowned whatever contradicts the Book of God
Al-Sadiq called the dual in Qur'an 5:95 an error of the kuttab
Al-Gulpaygani first reads the alif of the dual in Qur'an 5:95 as a scribe's addition, then judges the dual correct on Zurara's report
Ibn Abbas called tasta'nisu in Qur'an 24:27 a scribe's error
These reports mean an error of choice among the seven ahruf
The Mushaf of Fatimah holds no letter of the Qur'an
Ali ﵇ gathered the Qur'an after the Prophet's ﷺ burial, and the people refused it
Asim's reading never departed from al-Sulami's, nor al-Sulami's from Ali's ﵇
Had Uthman not made the codices, Ali ﵇ would have
Parchment of the Birmingham leaves dates to 568-645 CE
The Qur'an God sent down is what lies between the two covers, and whoever says the Imamis hold more is a liar
The Qur'an now in Muslim hands has no addition and no loss
The Qur'an in hand is incomplete, and the whole exists preserved with "its people"
